facts.statement: The genus Dineobellator is known from a single species, Dineobellator notohesperus, represented by a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Dineobellator notohesperus, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, designated SMP VP-2430, was first recovered in 2008 from the Ojo Alamo Formation by Robert M. Sullivan, Steven E. Jasinski, and James Nikas.
facts.quote: The holotype remains are designated SMP VP-2430 and were first recovered in 2008 from the Ojo Alamo Formation by Robert M. Sullivan, Steven E. Jasinski and James Nikas.

facts.statement: The genus was formally named and described in 2020 by Steven E. Jasinski, Robert M. Sullivan, and Peter Dodson.
facts.quote: In 2020, by Jasinski, Sullivan and Peter Dodson.

facts.statement: Dineobellator possessed unique skeletal features including greater flexion in its hands and feet, tighter grip strength in its hand claws, and increased movement at the tail base compared to other dromaeosaurs.
facts.quote: Unique features of the skeleton suggest greater hand and feet flexion than normal for dromaeosaurs, a tighter grip strength in the manual unguals, and greater movement at the tail base.

facts.statement: Quill knobs found on the ulna indicate that Dineobellator was feathered.
facts.quote: Additionally, the presence of quill knobs on the ulna suggest it was feathered, as assumed for all dromaeosaurids.

facts.statement: Dineobellator lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) in the Ojo Alamo Formation of New Mexico, United States.
facts.quote: Dineobellator (meaning Diné warrior, pronounced ) is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) Ojo Alamo Formation (Naashoibito Member) of New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: Dineobellator lived approximately 67 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Dineobellator notohesperus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Dineobellator ("guerrero diné") de dinosaurio terópodo dromeosáurido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 67 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy América del Norte.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dineobellator were found in Maastrichtian sediments of the Naashoibito Member of the Ojo Alamo Formation in New Mexico, USA.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron hallados en sedimentos de la época del Maastrichtiense en el Miembro Naashoibito de la Formación Ojo Álamo, en Nuevo México, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Dineobellator lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian epoch.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: A gouge on a right-hand claw of the type specimen suggests an injury caused by a similarly sized theropod, possibly another Dineobellator.
facts.quote: One of the claws on the right hand of the type specimen of Dineobellator bears a gouge, the size of which is consistent with the claws of a similarly-sized theropod, possibly another Dineobellator.

facts.statement: The lack of healing on a claw gouge suggests the injury occurred near death, while a broken and re-healed rib indicates a previous injury survived by the individual.
facts.quote: No evidence of healing is present, suggesting that the injury occurred close to the time of death. A broken and re-healed rib was also documented in the specimen.

facts.statement: Dineobellator measured approximately 2 meters in length and is estimated to have weighed between 18 and 22 kilograms.
facts.quote: Dineobellator medía cerca de 2 metros de longitud y se cree que pesaría entre 18 a 22 kg.

facts.statement: The classification of Dineobellator is debated; it was initially placed in Velociraptorinae in 2020 but later reexamined in 2022 as a member of Eudromaeosauria outside the Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: In their 2020 phylogenetic analysis, Jasinski et al. recovered Dineobellator in the Velociraptorinae. In a 2022 reexamination of the holotype, Jasinski et al. instead recovered Dineobellator as a member of the Eudromaeosauria, outside of the Velociraptorinae, Saurornitholestinae and Dromaeosaurinae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Dineobellator within the subfamily Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético sitúa a Dineobellator en la subfamilia Velociraptorinae.

facts.statement: Dineobellator lived in southern Laramidia, an environment characterized by lush floodplains, wetlands, and riparian gymnosperm forests.
facts.quote: Dineobellator is part of the Ojo Alamo Formation fauna in southern Laramidia, at the time a lush floodplain dominated by wetlands and riparian gymnosperm forests.

facts.statement: The top predators in Dineobellator's ecosystem were the azhdarchid pterosaur Quetzalcoatlus and the tyrannosaur Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The top predators of the formation's ecosystem were the azhdarchid pterosaur Quetzalcoatlus and Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The presence of Dineobellator suggests that dromaeosaurs occupied discrete ecological niches as active predators even alongside large tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The presence of a dromaeosaur suggests that the dromaeosaurs were active predators that had discrete ecological niches even in the presence of large tyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: At least eight types of mammals and seven types of turtles from the formation are inferred to have been common prey items for Dineobellator.
facts.quote: Entre tanto, hay al menos 8 tipos de mamíferos de esta formación, tales como Alphadon, Essonodon, Mesodma, y Meniscoessus, además de siete tipos de tortugas, Aspideretoides, Compsemys, Hoplochelys, Neurankylus, Plastomenus, y posiblemente Adocus y a Basilemys, todos los cuales se infiere que eran presas comunes para Dineobellator.
